summary: Follow-up call from Amey Sorval (Akarparna Gruharekha) to Prajakta Kerdule about the ₹16.5 lakh (tax included) interior proposal for her three-bedroom flat on the fourth floor of Parnakunj Nivas; the quotation wrongly showed the third floor, her sister's flat. She had already given the work to Naksharekha Hastakam (owner Kedar Verkhede) at ₹11.8 lakh including tax, against her ₹12 lakh budget, for a kitchen and two wardrobes, with a 20% advance of ₹2,36,000 paid yesterday, work starting 5 November and completion six weeks from material arrival. Her reasons: the budget gap, the team resisting her request to drop dining storage, and too many follow-up calls. Amey offered a revised scope sheet and milestone changes, and at the end a ₹1 lakh discount, which she refused as the deal is closed. He gave a practical checklist for verifying hardware and materials without judging the other contractor, disowned a colleague's remark that local work fails within a year, and agreed not to contact her contractor. Her ₹10,000 design deposit is non-refundable and covered site measurement and two layouts; he will send the measurement sheet, both layouts, the receipt and invoice (in her husband Nikhil Kerdule's name) and the checklist in one message by 6 pm today. No publishing of her plans, no further sales calls, and no future callback unless she asks. Recorded as lost.

strengths.title: Practical checklist without judging the competitor
strengths.explanation: When Prajakta asked for help verifying thickness, edges and hinges but no sales pitch, you gave neutral steps (match material samples with the bill, sign internal divisions on the drawing) and said you cannot judge their quality without seeing it. You also disowned your colleague's 'local work fails within a year' remark. This is how to leave a lost customer with respect for your brand.

strengths.title: Stopped follow-ups and delivered what she paid for
strengths.explanation: You agreed to stop sales calls and office follow-ups, set no future callback without her permission, and committed to send the measurement sheet, both layouts, receipt and invoice by 6 pm. You also confirmed no publishing of her plans, no contact with her contractor and no change to the invoice name.

strengths.title: Asked for loss reasons and owned the gap
strengths.explanation: You asked where the difference felt largest without pressure, admitted 'मी price सांगत बसलो, पण तुमच्या priority चं नीट version दिलं नाही', and that the team treated her dining-storage cut as a design preference rather than a budget decision. You confirmed the three reasons for the record.

improvements.title: Scope cut resisted instead of adapting to the budget
improvements.explanation: Prajakta's budget was ₹12 lakh against ₹16.5 lakh. When she said she did not need dining storage, your team told her the design would look bad, and the proposal came back as a big package even though the first survey had captured her actual needs, including space around her mother's old chair. In proposals, treat every 'we don't need this' as a budget instruction: 'ठीक आहे, dining storage काढतो; budget मध्ये बसणारं version पाठवतो.'

improvements.title: Reopened price after a clear, final decision
improvements.explanation: She said the work was given elsewhere and the advance was paid. You still offered a revised sheet, milestone changes, and at the end a ₹1 lakh discount. She said 'पुन्हा तिथेच गेलो आपण'. Once a buyer confirms a paid commitment, close cleanly: 'समजलं, निर्णय स्वीकारतो. Files पाठवतो.'

improvements.title: Quotation showed the wrong floor
improvements.explanation: The quotation listed the third floor, her sister's flat, instead of her fourth floor. She called it a small detail that still made her worry. Check the address and unit details on every quotation before it goes out.

objection_analysis.title: Budget gap: defended value first
objection_analysis.explanation: Your first reply to the ₹16.5 lakh against ₹12 lakh gap was a defence of supervisors and drawings. On a lost-deal call, acknowledge first; you did get there in your next turn.

objection_analysis.title: Competitor comparison
objection_analysis.explanation: Asking whether the ₹11.8 lakh included tax and comparable scope was fair, but she had no interest in a new presentation; the scopes differ (kitchen and two wardrobes against your fuller package).

objection_analysis.title: Concern about the team's attitude to local contractors
objection_analysis.explanation: She was irritated by a colleague's claim that local work fails within a year. You said it was wrong and offered to share her feedback internally without names.

objection_analysis.title: Design deposit and missing layout
objection_analysis.explanation: You stated clearly what the ₹10,000 covered and that it is non-refundable, and accepted that the second layout PDF was still owed.

objection_analysis.title: Follow-up fatigue
objection_analysis.explanation: She received repeated calls from you and the office. You accepted that the notes did not match and stopped all sales calls.

closing_analysis.title: Clean loss record after one unnecessary reopen
closing_analysis.explanation: After the ₹1 lakh offer was refused, you admitted reopening price was unnecessary, closed the record as lost and read back the three reasons; she confirmed them and asked that the design not be recorded as bad.

closing_analysis.title: Single delivery message
closing_analysis.explanation: Files, receipt, invoice and checklist in one message by 6 pm; she will acknowledge receipt, and calls only if she reports a problem.

verdict: The deal was lost before this call, mainly because the proposal did not adapt to a ₹12 lakh budget and the team resisted her scope cut. On this call Amey handled the loss well: honest reasons, a neutral checklist, delivery of the paid documents and an end to follow-ups. The weakness was trying to reopen the deal three times after a paid commitment.

dimensions.observation: Respectful listening and admissions (s7, s27, s39) left her wanting good relations (s58). Repeated reopening (s13, s17, s55) strained that.
Good loss discovery on this call (s3, s9). The earlier process lost her usage needs between survey and proposal (s47, s49).
Her ₹12 lakh budget was known (s4), yet the proposal stayed at ₹16.5 lakh with scope she had rejected (s6).
Her priority was usability over looks and keeping debt low (s4, s16); the proposal sold a fuller design instead.
Package size and the wrong floor in the quotation (s8, s47) signalled that she had not been heard.
Strong on the competitor and colleague's remark (s25, s27); defensive at first on budget (s5).
Three reopen attempts after a paid commitment (s13, s17, s55), then a clean, confirmed loss closure (s57-s59).
Clear, courteous wording, and he confirmed what she said after a bad line (s45-s46). Voice tone cannot be judged from text.

diagnosis.text: Lost on budget fit and not listening to a scope cut; this call protected the relationship but kept reaching for a deal that was already closed.

outcome.text: Lost to Naksharekha Hastakam with an advance paid; recorded as lost. Documents by 6 pm today; no further sales contact unless she asks.

missing_inputs: How often proposals exceed the stated budget
Number of losses linked to rejected scope cuts

strength_details.why_it_matters: Helping a lost buyer verify her contractor without attacking them builds a reputation that brings referrals.
Delivering what the ₹10,000 paid for and stopping calls ends the relationship on her terms, which she explicitly valued.
Specific loss reasons let the team fix the proposal process rather than blaming price.

what_happened.text: She asked to drop dining storage and was told the design would look bad; the proposal came back as a large package.

improvement_details.why_it_matters: A buyer who feels unheard chooses the vendor who fits her budget, even if she liked your design.
improvement_details.replacement_behavior: Send a version that removes what she rejected and fits her budget, with optional add-ons listed separately.

what_happened.text: After she confirmed an advance and start date, you offered a ₹1 lakh discount.

improvement_details.why_it_matters: Reopening a closed decision confirms her complaint about being pushed and risks the goodwill you had rebuilt.
improvement_details.replacement_behavior: Once a paid commitment is confirmed, accept the decision and move to handover only.

what_happened.text: The quotation had the third floor instead of her fourth floor.

improvement_details.why_it_matters: Small errors make a buyer doubt the care that will go into her home.
improvement_details.replacement_behavior: Check name, project, wing and floor on every quotation before sending.

golden_moments.why_effective: Refusing to judge unseen work while giving useful checks showed integrity at the moment of loss.
Stopping sales calls and leaving contact to her answered her main frustration in one line.

source.text: She said if she had been heard and given options, the conversation would have been different.

prospect_interpretations.possible_concern: The loss may be more about feeling unheard than about the rupee gap alone.

source.text: She mentioned future third-room work but asked not to be treated as a lead.

prospect_interpretations.possible_concern: Any unsolicited contact would close the door; she may return only if left alone.

rewatch.text: ₹1 lakh discount offered after a final decision.
Neutral checklist without judging the competitor.

before.text: You offered a ₹1 lakh discount; she refused and said the deal is closed.

change.text: You admitted reopening price was unnecessary and closed the record as lost with her reasons.

after.text: She confirmed the reasons, said she liked the design and wants no bad relations.

conversation_change.possible_effect: Accepting the decision may have restored goodwill after the discount attempt.

ethics_notes.text: Committed not to publish her home plans without separate permission and not to contact her contractor.

next_call_focus.behavior: Treat a buyer's scope cuts as budget instructions and send a version that fits the stated budget.
next_call_focus.target: On the next proposal where the budget is below the full package, send a budget-fit version with optional add-ons listed separately.

practice.instructions: Take this proposal and rebuild it to fit ₹12 lakh using only her stated needs (kitchen, two wardrobes, no dining storage, space for the chair). Review it with your manager.
practice.success_condition: The rebuilt version fits the budget and every removed item matches something she said she did not need.

final_assessment.repeat: Graceful loss handling: neutral checklist, delivering paid documents, stopping follow-ups.
final_assessment.fix_first: Adapt proposals to stated budgets and scope cuts.
final_assessment.next_focus: Do not reopen price after a buyer confirms a paid commitment elsewhere.
final_assessment.assessment: Deal lost on fit and listening; the relationship was handled well at the end.
